Compared with December, the January 29, 2020 FOMC statement balances a strong labor market with below-target inflation and weak business investment/exports while holding the funds rate at 1.50–1.75%. In Taylor-rule terms (as in Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), sub-2% inflation and anchored expectations justify staying on hold with a symmetric 2% objective. Continuing Treasury bill purchases and repo operations to keep “ample reserves” aligns with floor-system implementation via interest on reserves (Goodfriend, 2002) and is more technical than QE, conveying a modestly dovish but not aggressive easing signal. A flatter Phillips curve (evidence from core non-tradables) helps explain low unemployment alongside muted inflation, reducing the case for preemptive hikes. Weak capex despite low rates points to non-rate headwinds rather than interest-rate “crowding out,” which tempers the positivity. Overall tone: slightly positive/dovish.
